answer: Agents deposit bonded stake and, at each epoch, evaluate a committed polynomial over their registered identity, using Semaphore membership proofs and RLN rate-limit nullifiers to bind messages to one secret. A duplicate message yields two valid shares at the same point; Shamir interpolation reconstructs the private key, enabling instantaneous, proof-based collateral slashing. Thus identities named opal, gale, or summit cannot multiply one stake-backed quota.
